newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY AS MAJOR TURNS BUYER.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY AS MAJOR TURNS BUYER.

text.p: Euro high sulphur fuel oil barges steadied late on Thursday after a major entered the market as buyer at higher numbers, while tighter supply in both high and low sulphur cargoes kept their levels notionally strong.
High sulphur barges were traded at $95 and $95.50 a tonne fob ARA, or about Wednesday's closing level, after earlier trades at $94 a tonne.

Traders said that the lower figures were done as the market eased with loading delays at two key storage sites said to have ended, but many traders maintained that prompt material remains in low supply.
But then a major looking to cover commitments entered the market as a buyer at $95, achieved with some difficulty due to lower supply, followed by a trader that bought at $0.5 a tonne higher.
"If you are looking for prompt material, little is available," one trader said. Another trader said that only material loading after August 11 could be readily bought.

High sulphur cracked cargoes were quiet but reportedly talked steady to a little stronger on the offer side at about $94/$95 cif, with buyers some $4 lower. Traders said supply of non-Russian material were very low.

A trader was offering Russian M-100 cracked at two means plus $2, but others said that a deal could be effected at 50-70 cents a tonne less. One seller was offering cracked M-100 at $4 over the two means quote -- a price deemed too high by most market players.
An independent trader said that the first of several cargoes of Russian M-100 he is receiving soon has arrived today -- with all destined to the barge market.
"I can sell them as cargoes, but with barges at $95 I will be happy to sell them as barges," the trader added. The second cargo arrives on Friday, and the third and fourth next week.
One percent was quiet but sellers were bullish, saying that there were few cargoes left on the market and swaps were still holding at the $96/$97 level.
"I have a cargo which I can sell or keep. I'll be looking for a floating number but if I'd to sell in terms of a fixed number, I'd be looking at $96/$97," a trader with a major said.
"It is a fairly tight market on the supply side," he added.
Low sulphur barges were still offered at strong numbers, unchanged from a day earlier, at $97/$98 but no deals were clinched.
